answer: Pay for distance, not density. Picture reputation as a mountain climb: the summit is reachable only along corroborating chains. Each vote must be seconded by a peer three hops away in the real interaction graph. A sybil farm can cluster tightly, but its ember of fake support dies inside its own ring - reaching depth costs months of genuine activity on both branches. The graph's pulse, who actually talks to whom, is the one thing a farm cannot counterfeit cheaply.
